# `mutable-pointer-parameter`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports a `*T` parameter whose pointee is only read.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`*const T` documents the callee's contract and allows callers to pass immutable
values.

## When it fires

It skips callbacks, `deinit*` and `destroy*` conventions, escaping addresses,
mutable captures, loops, and other cases where indirect mutation is uncertain.
A member handed whole to a call (other than `assert` and by-value builtins), or
bound to a local or capture that is then mutated through or handed on, counts
as a possible mutation: it may be a nested pointer or a handle, as in
`c.destroy(self.handle)`, that the function changes state through.

`pub` and `export` functions are not reported. Their signature is API that
other files may pin where this file cannot see it (a vtable entry, a callback
field, a function-pointer type), and promising never to mutate is the API
owner's decision.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn total(p: *u32) u32 {
    return p.* + 1;
}
```
